question: Haven — DEF, spike planted A, you are the last defender in a 1v3 with a Bulldog near A Lobby, ~20s left. The three attackers are holding their post-plant. Can you even win this, and how?

options.label: Isolate one fight: hold a tight angle they must clear, win the 1v1 you create, then reassess the defuse
options.explication_courte: A 1v3 retake is won by never fighting more than one at a time. Use the geometry of A to catch a single attacker off his crossfire, win that duel to make it a 1v2, and let their own post-plant spread work against them.

sources_option.citation: In a lopsided retake, isolate one attacker at a time using site geometry rather than challenging the whole post-plant at once

options.label: Rush onto site and start defusing immediately to force them to show themselves
options.explication_courte: Running straight onto a spike three attackers are watching gets you killed before the defuse bar fills. You have to clear at least some of them first; a naked defuse in a 1v3 is a donation.

sources_option.citation: Defusing while enemies still hold the spike is only viable after clearing or forcing them off; a contested defuse needs cover or a cleared angle

options.label: Use the clock: delay, reposition, and bait them into over-rotating or pushing you one by one
options.explication_courte: Playing time and repositioning is smart to force isolation — but with only ~20s you can't stall forever; the clock that protects the plant is now the attackers' friend, so passive delay alone eventually just runs out.

sources_option.citation: Time pressure cuts both ways on a retake; use repositioning to isolate, but remember the defuse clock forces you to act

options.label: Wide-swing into A site spraying the Bulldog to try to catch all three grouped
options.explication_courte: Swinging into three post-planted crosshairs is an instant death — you show to all of them at once and lose before you land a burst. The one thing that makes a 1v3 winnable, isolation, is exactly what this throws away.

sources_option.citation: Swinging into multiple players holding a site simultaneously is a losing duel; isolate rather than challenging the group

explication_longue: A 1v3 retake with the spike down and ~20 seconds left is hard but not hopeless — and the whole margin lives in one word: isolation. Three attackers holding a post-plant are strong together and weak apart, so your job as the last defender near A Lobby is to use Haven's geometry to only ever face one of them at a time. Hold or bait a tight angle a single attacker has to clear to keep eyes on the spike, win that 1v1, and now it's a 1v2 with their own spread working against them. What you cannot do is rush the spike and defuse in the open — three crosshairs are watching it and the defuse bar never fills before you die. Playing the clock and repositioning is a genuine tool to manufacture that isolation, but it can't be the whole plan: with ~20 seconds the defuse timer that used to protect the plant now works for the attackers, so pure passive delay eventually just expires. And wide-swinging into all three with the Bulldog is the fastest possible loss — you expose yourself to every gun at once and throw away the isolation that is your only path. Pick one fight, win it, then re-solve the round.

sources.citation: Win lopsided retakes by isolating attackers one at a time with site geometry and clearing before any defuse attempt
